proposals: The Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell should publish India's annual LNG imports in million tonnes on the same basis as the International Gas Union's global trade measure, so that India's share of the record 437 Mt can be read directly rather than converted from differently defined Indian series.

GAIL, Petronet LNG and other Indian buyers should disclose, for each new long-term LNG purchase agreement, the supplying liquefaction project and whether it uses gas-turbine or electric drive, so that the decades-long lock-in this post describes in the 2021–25 sanctioning wave is visible in what India contracts.

The Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell should publish an annual average landed price for India's LNG imports split between long-term contract and spot cargoes, so that the price and contract-structure comparison this post could not attempt over the decade is possible for India at least.
